fintech.title: Revolut CEO Nik Storonsky says company wants to “dominate” the US (10 minute podcast)
fintech.summary: Revolut CEO Nik Storonsky says the fintech plans to build a full US digital banking offering, including credit cards and loans, as it competes with incumbents such as JPMorgan and American Express. He also expects AI and automation to reshape banking, with Revolut preparing to test AI agents that can shop and transact on behalf of customers.

fintech.title: Netflix sets Nov. 19 release for FTX drama “The Altruists”
fintech.summary: Netflix will release “The Altruists,” a dramatized series about the collapse of FTX, on November 19, starring Anthony Boyle as Sam Bankman-Fried and Julia Garner as Caroline Ellison. The show focuses on their relationship and the effective altruism movement surrounding FTX, turning one of crypto's biggest scandals into a scripted Hollywood drama.

fintech.title: OpenAI's annualized revenue reportedly closer to $50B, not $70B
fintech.summary: OpenAI has reportedly told investors that annualized revenue is approaching $50 billion, well below the roughly $70 billion figure previously circulated by investors attempting to compare the company with Anthropic. The discrepancy also highlights differing revenue definitions between the two companies, while raising more scrutiny around OpenAI's economics as it invests heavily in infrastructure and prepares for a potential IPO in 2027.

fintech.title: You need a new CFO
fintech.summary: AI is changing finance software from tools that help teams manage work into systems that increasingly do the work themselves, pushing CFOs toward a new role as builders of the company's operating system. The AI-native finance organization is smaller and higher leverage, with continuous forecasting, finance engineers, agent-driven workflows, and stronger audit controls, while the CFO focuses more on designing what people versus software should do and less on manually collecting and reconciling data.

fintech.title: Where will banks make money if it isn't from payments?
fintech.summary: AI agents and programmable money are pushing financial value away from transaction processing and toward orchestration, identity, liquidity, compliance, and software. McKinsey estimates agentic AI could put $75 billion to $160 billion of payments revenue at risk by 2030, while Capgemini says $230 billion is already exposed across areas like FX spreads, correspondent fees, and float income. The emerging battleground is increasingly about who controls the intelligence that decides how money moves, whether that is a bank, fintech, software platform, or AI agent.

fintech.title: Payment Infrastructure Your Startup Can Plan On
fintech.summary: Bring ACH, wires, instant payments, checks, push-to-card, and stablecoins into your product with one API. With Modern Treasury, you get accounts, ledgering, payments, and compliance built in. See Modern Treasury's usage-based pricing and start building .

fintech.title: Chase adds payroll to larger business banking offering
fintech.summary: Powered by Gusto, the service lets eligible small businesses handle payroll, tax filings, and employee payments inside Chase Business Online, with next-day processing available to qualifying checking customers. The integration brings another essential workflow into Chase's platform while leaving the specialized payroll calculations and filings to its fintech partner.

fintech.title: Experian unveils new consumer reporting agency for cashflow underwriting
fintech.summary: Experian is building an FCRA-regulated layer that lets lenders incorporate permissioned bank-account activity into credit decisions, potentially helping thin-file and credit-challenged borrowers qualify. Experian says these insights can increase approvals by up to 25% without changing risk tolerance, while bringing consent, data aggregation, standardized reports, analytics, and its existing scoring tools into one ecosystem. The move puts Experian into closer competition with Plaid, Prism Data, Mastercard Finicity, and Nova Credit, even as Plaid remains one of its data partners.

fintech.title: NFL tells Supreme Court prediction market sports contracts are gambling, not swaps
fintech.summary: The NFL urged the Supreme Court to review whether sports prediction contracts such as Kalshi's should be regulated as gambling by states or as swaps under exclusive CFTC jurisdiction, arguing that Dodd-Frank was not intended to federalize sports betting. The dispute has produced conflicting appeals-court rulings, while Kalshi argues its markets are federally regulated and protected by existing integrity controls, setting up a potentially important Supreme Court test of prediction-market regulation.

fintech.title: Amex dinged by Fed, OCC over anti-money laundering failures
fintech.summary: American Express National Bank was ordered to pay a $350 million penalty after the OCC found major deficiencies in its anti-money laundering program, including weak risk assessments and systemic failures in suspicious activity monitoring that regulators said involved roughly $13 billion of suspected money laundering activity over 10 years. The Federal Reserve separately issued a cease-and-desist order covering broader enterprise-wide AML issues, while Amex said the penalty will not affect its 2026 or 2027 guidance.

fintech.title: Wall Street banks launch record $60bn chip deal for Broadcom and Anthropic
fintech.summary: Bank of America, Citi, and Morgan Stanley are syndicating $42 billion of Broadcom-backed senior loans plus $18 billion of riskier junior debt to finance Anthropic's lease of Google-designed chips.

fintech.title: Citi-backed fintech Capitolis valued at $1.9B in latest funding round
fintech.summary: Capitolis raised $220 million in new financing at a $1.9 billion valuation, including a $120 million Series E led by Citi with participation from Bank of America, Nomura, Tradeweb, and several major global banks.

fintech.title: JPMorgan tops global AI banking index with jobs seen to grow
fintech.summary: AI capabilities across banking improved nearly three times faster over the past year than the average of the previous three years, as deployment accelerated at a record pace.

it.title: The 7 keys to making sense of AI priorities as a C-suite leader
it.summary: You're absolutely flooded with AI predictions. How do you know what matters most? Gartner's 2.4k+ analysts have worked on over 4k AI use cases and case studies. This on-demand webinar breaks down: The 7 strategic AI themes Gartner believes will have the greatest impact on organizations over the next 12 months Why these themes matter across the C-suite and require leaders to align on risk, opportunities and priorities The actions executives should consider today and the role each function will play in 2027 Explore the AI hub for the full range of Gartner's AI insights

it.title: HPE's networking boss says AI will handle all trouble tickets without humans in two years
it.summary: HPE networking chief Rami Rahim predicts that AI-driven network operations could eliminate the need for human intervention in troubleshooting tickets within two years. He estimates that 70-80% of tickets already require no human intervention, reflecting HPE's push toward autonomous enterprise network management following its acquisition of Juniper Networks.

it.title: Global PC shipments crater 20% as rising prices hammer demand
it.summary: Global PC shipments fell roughly 20% year-over-year in Q3 2026 as rising memory costs and earlier purchasing pushed demand lower. AI infrastructure's appetite for components is contributing to higher PC prices, potentially complicating corporate device refresh cycles and hardware budgets.

it.title: Nvidia in talks to invest further in Reflection AI or buy it
it.summary: Nvidia is in talks to acquire or deepen its investment in US-based open-weight model start-up Reflection AI. Discussions are at an early stage and could result in an acqui-hire to avoid drawn-out regulatory reviews. Reflection AI was reportedly seeking funding at a $25 billion pre-money valuation earlier this year, and Nvidia has already invested $800 million in the company.

it.title: Self-improving software is inevitable
it.summary: AI coding agents currently automate writing code, but the feedback loop of identifying issues and deciding what to fix remains largely manual. Connecting production signals such as logs, traces, and support tickets to AI agents through clearly defined performance goals could enable software to continuously identify problems and implement improvements, shifting engineers toward defining objectives and overseeing outcomes.

it.title: Fast AI, slow rollback: the risk facing Apple IT teams
it.summary: A Fleet survey found that 86% of IT teams allow AI-generated configurations or scripts into production, but 69% cannot roll back a problematic change within an hour. The findings highlight a growing operational challenge as endpoint management automation advances faster than change control and recovery capabilities.

it.title: Neoclouds and the enterprises that need them
it.summary: Specialized GPU cloud providers such as CoreWeave, Lambda, and Nebius are growing rapidly as demand for AI infrastructure increases. These providers must better explain how their services fit into enterprise architecture alongside traditional hyperscalers, particularly around integration, governance, and operational responsibility.

it.title: How agents unlock new markets
it.summary: AI agents can unlock new markets by reducing negotiation and coordination costs, enabling transactions that were previously uneconomical or impossible. Unlike consumer-side agents that merely select from existing static offers, future agentic markets will involve buyer and seller agents collaborating to construct entirely new agreements and uncover latent supply and demand.

it.title: Redis asked 1,000 AI leaders about context. 97% call it critical, yet only 4% are ready.
it.summary: 81% of organizations still handle context ad hoc, and 56% say reaching production took longer than expected. The State of Context Engineering report breaks down what production‑ready context requires and where teams get stuck. Redis's Maturity Model shows where you stand. Download it to benchmark your team.

it.title: Google brings agentic AI to Gemini, starting with businesses
it.summary: Google introduced a new enterprise Gemini agent that can independently plan and execute multi-step tasks across Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Jira, and other business applications. The agent can have its own workplace identity, email address, and audit trail, positioning it as a digital coworker rather than a traditional chatbot.

it.title: Cloudflare acquires Deno to improve its Workers programming model
it.summary: Cloudflare announced it is acquiring Deno to improve its Workers programming model and platform. The company plans to use the acquisition to enhance its network software capabilities, noting that Deno recently launched an open-source implementation of Workers called celld.

it.title: Microsoft will let Copilot act on local files on Windows PCs
it.summary: Microsoft announced new Copilot capabilities that will allow the assistant to organize files, change settings, and execute tasks directly on Windows PCs with user permission. The company is also introducing hybrid AI processing that combines local and cloud models, potentially improving privacy, performance, and costs for enterprise users.

it.title: Cisco brings collaborative agents and Claude into Webex chats
it.summary: Cisco is adding collaborative AI agents to Webex conversations, allowing employees to assign tasks, summarize discussions, and coordinate work directly within group chats. The update also introduces integrations with Anthropic's Claude agents, a personalized workspace, and AI-assisted calling features.

it.title: Atlas Infinite: MongoDB's Disaggregated Architecture
it.summary: MongoDB released Atlas Infinite in public preview alongside MongoDB 9.0, introducing a compute-storage disaggregated architecture designed to separate scaling while preserving WiredTiger's performance and security. To keep customer data encrypted and maintain WiredTiger's batching efficiency, MongoDB developed a blind shared storage layer using two separate logs and page materializers rather than traditional physical page logging.

it.title: LibreOffice touts ‘no AI' as a feature
it.summary: LibreOffice's developers are positioning the absence of built-in AI as a deliberate product choice, emphasizing privacy, user control, and open standards. The project remains open to future AI capabilities, provided they are optional and meet its requirements for transparency and data ownership.

it.title: Windows 11 gains ground as price hike looms for Windows 10 security updates
it.summary: Windows 11 now accounts for an estimated 71.5% of Windows PCs, while the annual cost of extended Windows 10 security updates for businesses is set to double to $122 per device.

it.title: Bidding war over key component could eliminate third hard disk maker
it.summary: Seagate and Toshiba are reportedly competing to acquire TDK's hard disk head business, potentially reshaping the already highly concentrated storage hardware market.

it.title: A versioned filesystem for disposable sandboxes
it.summary: The system behaves like database transactions and Git commits by utilizing copy-on-write snapshots, content-addressing, and atomic compare-and-swap operations on pointers.

hardware.title: Oxide Computer Company Secures $445M Series D Funding Round
hardware.summary: Who's building on-prem compute in 2026? It turns out a lot of people! Oxide Computer Company, which builds custom on-prem cloud compute systems, has closed a massive $445 million Series D funding round led by Eclipse, with participation from major investors including Jane Street, Atreides Management, and chipmaker AMD. The capital injection follows the startup achieving operational profitability and will be used to scale manufacturing capacity, secure raw material inventory, and fulfill a rapidly expanding order backlog for their commercial cloud computer racks.

hardware.title: SpaceX buys 800 MHz low-band spectrum to pair terrestrial towers with 2 GHz Starlink satellites
hardware.summary: SpaceX agreed to buy up to 14 MHz of paired 800 MHz low-band spectrum, which penetrates buildings, and plans to deploy its own antennas on towers and rooftops to use it, with most existing phones already supporting the band. Separately, the FCC approved 15,000 more Starlink satellites optimized for 2 GHz. Together they point to a hybrid network, terrestrial indoors and satellite beyond towers. The deal needs FCC approval, and Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile shares fell roughly 6% on the news.

hardware.title: The Machines That Make the Machines: Advancing Industrial Digital Twins
hardware.summary: In this rare peek under the hood, we get a glimpse of how Foxconn uses NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac, and Metropolis platforms to create physically accurate digital twins of manufacturing facilities that assemble next-generation AI server hardware. By simulating factory layouts, automated optical inspection systems, and autonomous mobile robot fleets in virtual environments before physical deployment, the company minimizes factory commissioning delays and boosts production efficiency. This approach showcases how system architects and automation specialists can leverage high-fidelity simulation to safely validate and optimize complex robotic workcells prior to hardware installation.

hardware.title: Blue Origin rebuilds LC-36 for vertical New Glenn integration, targeting a December return
hardware.summary: After May's pad explosion destroyed its transporter-erector, Blue Origin is rebuilding LC-36 for vertical integration, loading New Glenn through the support tower alone, as with Starship. Crews destacked the tower, added cryogenic propellant plumbing on the ground, and have begun restacking modules, while the launch bridge is restored. Umbilicals and fairing access platforms haven't appeared yet. Bezos targets a December return to flight carrying Blue Ring, though he joked it could slip to December 31.

hardware.title: Photonic chips learn after fabrication by measuring their own optical gradients
hardware.summary: A Nature Computational Science briefing describes an in situ learning method where photonic integrated circuits directly measure optical gradients, so diverse circuit layouts can be trained after they're built. That removes the need for a full digital model of the chip, which optical training normally leans on. The team demonstrated matrix design, multiwavelength computation, and rapid meta-learning on the hardware. Specifics like accuracy or energy figures aren't included.

hardware.title: ScaRF-SLAM: Scale-Consistent Reconstruction with Feed-Forward Models and Classical Visual SLAM
hardware.summary: ScaRF-SLAM is a dense visual mapping system that pairs the reliability of classical visual SLAM with modern feed-forward geometric foundation models for 3D scene reconstruction from the Oxford Robot Dynamics Lab. By decoupling camera tracking from dense depth estimation and optimizing scale consistency across submaps, it achieves globally accurate 3D maps across diverse sensor configurations. For perception engineers and autonomy developers, this framework provides a practical way to produce metric-scale environmental maps in real time without sacrificing tracking stability

hardware.title: Q8botOne: A Palm-Sized Open-Source Quadruped Robot with Smart Actuators
hardware.summary: ZeroWire Robotics has launched the Q8botOne, a smartphone-sized open-source quadruped robot featuring an innovative wire-free chassis where the main printed circuit board serves as the structural frame. Driven by an ESP32-C3 microcontroller and eight DYNAMIXEL smart bus actuators with parallel-linkage legs, the compact robot can walk, trot, jump, and carry twice its 250-gram payload.

hardware.title: Ledger confirms a hardware implant in a tampered wallet as suspected losses near $93M
hardware.summary: Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in one affected user's device, bought from Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, pointing to tampering after manufacturing rather than a breach of Ledger itself. Mark Karpelès published images of a modified Nano X with a small board behind the screen and cellular components, which would presumably capture the 24-word recovery phrase as it displays during setup, leaving the secure element untouched.

hardware.title: Super Micro “fixer” pleads guilty in $2.5B scheme to divert Nvidia servers to China
hardware.summary: Ting-Wei Sun pleaded guilty to four counts, including conspiracy to violate export controls, in a scheme that routed about $2.5 billion of Nvidia-powered servers through a Southeast Asian company to buyers in China.

hardware.title: ASML raises EUV and DUV spare parts prices 10% for Samsung and SK Hynix
hardware.summary: ASML will raise prices 10% on all EUV and DUV replacement parts supplied to South Korea starting with January 2027 deliveries, and Samsung and SK Hynix have accepted

hardware.title: Jumper: An Open-Source Crab Robot with Walking and Jumping Capabilities
hardware.summary: Jumper is an open-source biomimetic robot that replicates crab locomotion, combining sideways multi-legged walking with an explosive spring-assisted jumping mechanism.

hardware.title: EasyNav 0.5.0 Navigation System Released for ROS 2 Distributions
hardware.summary: EasyNav 0.5.0 has officially launched, delivering an accessible yet comprehensive open-source navigation stack with upgraded path planning, improved recovery behaviors, and reduced compute overhead for ROS 2 systems.
